newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul mulls change in arms purchase after scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul mulls change in arms purchase after scandal.

text.p: South Korea's new defence minister said on Monday his ministry was considering sweeping reforms in weapons procurement following an arms scandal involving his predecessor.
A ministry statement said such steps were necessary because of growing public doubt and mistrust over a programme to improve defence capability.
"Defence Minister Kim Dong-jin told parliament he was considering extraordinary measures for a massive surgery over the process," it said.
Earlier this month Kim succeeded Lee Yang-ho, who was arrested at the weekend on charges of bribery and leaking official secrets to an arms dealer.

State prosecutors said Lee had admitted during a probe that he accepted a 150 million won- ($181,000-) bribe last year from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd through the arms dealer, over a government purchase of military helicopters.
Lee and the arms dealer split a 300 million won-bribe from Daewoo Heavy to arrange the government purchase, they said.

Lee has not commented publicly on the charges, but state media earlier quoted him as denying any wrongdoing. Daewoo said it gave money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe.

The scandal has embarrassed President Kim Young-sam, who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption crusade that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being convicted in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both men are appealing.

The statement said the Defence Ministry would work out safeguards against corruption, such as the screening of arms dealers to exclude those who are not "patriotic, honest and trustworthy" from providing arms to the military.
